subject: mcc-acute-care
title: Hypoglycaemia and glucose emergencies

steps.tx: **Hypoglycaemia** is defined by a low **plasma glucose** that produces symptoms, or by any low reading accompanied by **neuroglycopenic** features. Symptoms fall into two groups. **Adrenergic** warning signs include sweating, tremor and palpitations, while **neuroglycopenic** features include confusion, drowsiness and coma. Recognising both groups matters because adrenergic signs alert the patient early, allowing treatment before the brain is affected.
steps.say: Hypoglycaemia is defined by a low plasma glucose that produces symptoms, or by any low reading accompanied by neuroglycopenic features. Symptoms fall into two groups. Adrenergic warning signs include sweating, tremor and palpitations, while neuroglycopenic features include confusion, drowsiness and coma. steps.tx: Treat by route according to consciousness and access. An **alert patient who can swallow** takes oral fast-acting carbohydrate, then glucose is rechecked. An **unresponsive patient** without intravenous access receives **intramuscular glucagon**. If intravenous access exists, a **dextrose bolus** is used. Glucagon works by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

rows: Oral carbohydrate only if swallowing is safe

steps.tx: Consider **drug and kidney factors** that prolong hypoglycaemia. **Sulfonylureas** and **insulin** stimulate or deliver glucose-lowering action that can outlast the first treatment. **Renal impairment** slows clearance of insulin and sulfonylureas, so glucose can fall again. Beta-blockers blunt adrenergic warning signs, so neuroglycopenic confusion may occur without sweating or tremor.
steps.say: Consider drug and kidney factors that prolong hypoglycaemia. Sulfonylureas and insulin can have a glucose-lowering effect that outlasts the first treatment. Renal impairment slows clearance of insulin and sulfonylureas, so glucose can fall again. Beta-blockers blunt adrenergic warning signs, so confusion may occur without sweating or tremor.

steps.tx: Use **factitious hypoglycaemia** as a diagnosis to consider when insulin is high but **C-peptide is suppressed**. Endogenous insulin is released with equal amounts of C-peptide, so a low C-peptide with high insulin points to an external source. Sulfonylurea screening is also useful in this setting. Insulinoma is the main endogenous cause and typically shows high C-peptide.

steps.tx: Before discharge, confirm that glucose is stable after the **first treatment** and that the cause has been identified. Patients on sulfonylureas with **renal impairment** or poor intake may need observation with serial glucose checks rather than discharge after one normal reading. Review the insulin or sulfonylurea dose and give carbohydrate advice with clinic follow-up.
